introduction.text: Piazza Navona is a historic public square in Rome built on the site of the 1st‑century AD Stadium of Domitian. It is renowned for its Baroque architecture, iconic fountains, and its role as a cultural gathering place.

history.description: The original stadium was constructed by Emperor Domitian in 80 AD.
The Fountain of Neptune (1574) and the Fountain of the Moor (1575) were created by Giacomo della Porta.
The Fountain of the Four Rivers (1651) was designed by Gian Lorenzo Bernini.
During the pontificate of Innocent X (1644‑1655) the piazza was transformed into a Baroque masterpiece.
From 1652 until 1866 the piazza was flooded on weekends in August for Pamphili family celebrations.
In 1869 the market was moved to Campo de' Fiori.
In September 2011 the Fountain of the Moor was damaged by vandalism.

design.description: The piazza exemplifies Baroque design with contributions from Bernini, Borromini, and other architects.

art.description: Bernini’s Fountain of the Four Rivers features four river gods and an obelisk.
The Fountain of the Moor displays a Moor wrestling with a dolphin.
The Fountain of Neptune, added in 1878, balances the Moor fountain.
